report:
Reviewed the fresh 17-line canonical_ownership claim, all four ordinary implementation associations, the complete two-entry associated test set, and captured dependencies. This assessment is for the revised claim, not the earlier unconditional cross-revision anonymous-identity guarantee.

Backend-authored paths and labels: src/inspector.rs builds local paths from the selected target and typed ownership segments, while SymbolReference stores path separately from label and presentation. build_symbol_directory, find_local_reference and InspectorReflectionResolver supply those references; selected_symbol and resolve_local_symbol compare supplied paths against represented ownership, rather than parsing display labels. canonical_external_reference uses the bridge's canonical_def_path, including crate stable ID, kind/name/disambiguator segments. resolve_external_path validates the exact root and every represented child prefix; nonexistent local/external symbols yield the provider's explicit symbol-not-found or product-not-found errors.

Entirely named ownership: symbol_identity_parts uses the symbol kind and percent-encoded name, not body detail, source span, ordinal sibling position or a Salsa handle. walk_symbols and canonical_children compose those segments under the owner path. Consequently unrelated/detail edits and distinct sibling movement do not change entirely named paths; rebuilding the host reconstructs those names. Rename/move/deletion removes the corresponding old chain and selection rejects it. External canonical paths derive from rustc definition ownership and stable crate IDs, with extern_crate_with_disambiguator rejecting a forged crate ID. Captured existing integration-test context contains named/associated navigation, reorder/rename and reconstruction checks plus an external forged-ID assertion; these are supplementary inspected context, not newly associated complete coverage.

Anonymous qualification: impl/header hashes, macro handles, anonymous external segments and duplicate occurrence suffixes remain navigation choices. The revised claim explicitly allows anonymous links and their descendants to change, disappear, or select another indistinguishable occurrence across edits/reconstruction. Thus the previously identified duplicate-deletion ambiguity and possible macro-handle movement are now documented limitations, not violations of the revised persistence guarantee. Within a fixed source revision canonical_children adds occurrence suffixes to equal local base segments and paths include their owner chain, maintaining distinct represented addresses; external paths include definition disambiguators. Unknown paths still fail explicitly. This review does not claim durable duplicate or macro identity across revisions.

Import identity: stable_symbol_hash's local-use branch hashes the flattened import count, normalized Path token spelling, binding-kind discriminant and the bound Name's text. It does not hash tracked handles or RelativeSpan. The associated Path::to_tokens implementation emits anchor and segment spelling; its StringSink dependency emits normalized separators/spacing. Captured UseImportCst/UseKind definitions confirm span is separate and binding kinds distinguish named, glob and unnamed imports. These four associated source files jointly cover the path generator and its normalization and external-path dependencies. Inspector navigation adds strings to reflection; it does not assign new semantic definition identities to imported routes. The bridge keeps structured_def_path (anonymous omitted) separate from canonical_def_path (anonymous included), preserving the distinct conformance projection.

Tests: the ordinary associated anonymous_use_paths_survive_sibling_reordering test visibly captures source products for two distinct imports, checks there are two, reverses their sibling order, and asserts both original paths still return their original source. It then opens an independent host, reverses module/import construction order, and repeats those assertions, exercising exclusion of position/database-local identity. This is a useful stronger guarantee for these distinct imports even though anonymous persistence generally remains best effort. During this review task's preceding implementation phase I executed cargo test --lib inspector::canonical_ownership_tests::anonymous_use_paths_survive_sibling_reordering -- --exact: the test first reproduced retargeting, and after the structural import correction passed (1 passed, 0 failed). cargo fmt and cargo build also passed then. No additional execution is claimed for this documentation-only follow-up.

The other associated entry, sage_meta::todo::crates_sage_inspector_inspection_canonical_ownership, is explicitly deferred and has no assertions. Its prerequisite is associating and reviewing the full local/anonymous/generated, reorder, rename, reconstruction, external parent/child/disambiguation and oracle-separation matrix. This remains justified deferred evidence rather than proof of those scenarios: move/deletion, same-revision duplicate-address distinction, forged child segments and broad generated/external scenarios are not established by the one ordinary associated regression. Accepting this declared gap does not upgrade the TODO to implemented test coverage. No N/A entries exist. All aspects of the revised claim are accounted for by source behavior or that explicit deferred test matrix; no required edit remains for the revised guarantee.
